blocks.text: Quick verdict

Proxy-Cheap is the better choice for low-cost scraping on easy and moderate targets where country or ISP targeting is enough: 10 GB costs about $7.80 at its promotional rate against $80 at Oxylabs pay-as-you-go. Oxylabs is the better choice when targets are hardened, when you need city or ZIP precision, when failed requests are expensive, or when procurement requires formal sourcing documentation and an SLA. Many teams use a cheap network for easy pages and a premium one for the hard ones.

Oxylabs and Proxy-Cheap represent the two extremes of the residential proxy market. Oxylabs is a premium enterprise vendor with a 175M+ pool, published 99.95% success rates and scraper APIs. Proxy-Cheap is a budget shop currently advertising rotating residential traffic at $0.78/GB with no plan. The price gap is roughly tenfold at small volumes, so the real question is what you lose by going cheap and which workloads justify paying for Oxylabs.

blocks.text: Oxylabs in 2026: what you get

Oxylabs is a Lithuanian web-data company and Bright Data's closest rival at the top of the market. It advertises a residential pool of more than 175 million IPs across 195 locations, publishes a 99.95% success rate for residential traffic, and sells seven product lines including datacenter, ISP and mobile proxies, a Web Scraper API and Web Unblocker. Onboarding is more sales-led than the mid-market providers, but self-service has expanded through 2026, including dedicated ISP proxies.

Strengths: One of the two largest residential pools available; Published 99.95% residential success rate; Strong scraper APIs that bill per result; Formal ethical-sourcing documentation for procurement. Weak spots: Expensive at low volume ($8/GB PAYG); Best rates need large monthly commitments; Residential trial goes through sales rather than self-service.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap has sold proxies since 2018 and says it serves 45,000+ customers. It offers seven product types: static residential (ISP) in IPv4 and IPv6, rotating residential, datacenter IPv4 and IPv6, and static and rotating mobile. Rotating residential is pure pay-as-you-go with no monthly plan, and the site claims coverage in 180+ countries. Targeting is mainly country and ISP level, and all products support SOCKS5 including UDP. It is a strong value pick, though independent benchmarks of its rotating pool have been mixed.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: Oxylabs vs Proxy-Cheap

Oxylabs charges $8/GB pay-as-you-go for residential traffic. Monthly plans start with Starter at $30 for 5 GB ($6/GB) and a Basic tier around $100 for 20 GB, and the rate falls to $2.50/GB on the $2,500/month Corporate plan. Mobile traffic starts at $7.50/GB.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

At 10 GB a month, Proxy-Cheap is the cheaper option at about $7.80 against $80 for Oxylabs, roughly 90% less. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Oxylabs does not publish an exact price for that volume; Proxy-Cheap comes to about $78. Both Oxylabs and Proxy-Cheap work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Proxy-Cheap does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. Oxylabs lists '175M+' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Oxylabs lists 195 countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, Oxylabs offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN, while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Oxylabs offers rotating and sticky sessions on residential and mobile, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: its pool size and Web Scraper API suit large crawls. How Proxy-Cheap compares: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed.

SERP and rank tracking: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: its scraper API returns parsed search results. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost.

Social media and multi-account management: Proxy-Cheap. Proxy-Cheap has the edge here. Why: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities. How Oxylabs compares: it works, but the pricing is built for volume, not a handful of accounts.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: city and ZIP targeting plus parsed e-commerce endpoints. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: fine for country-level price checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: broad geo coverage with ASN targeting. How Proxy-Cheap compares: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential.

Tight budgets: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. The limitation on the Oxylabs side: entry pricing is among the highest in this comparison.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Oxylabs: Residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. Oxylabs: Business verification on larger accounts. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Oxylabs and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Oxylabs and Proxy-Cheap is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Oxylabs: residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.

3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country. 4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Oxylabs comes out ahead in 4, Proxy-Cheap in 2, and 0 are ties. That makes Oxylabs the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Oxylabs is strongest for large scraping pipelines with steady volume, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
